newsitem.title: TAIWAN: FOCUS-Macronix enters high-stakes Taiwan chip war.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Macronix enters high-stakes Taiwan chip war.

text.p: Macronix International Co Ltd on Thursday became the sixth Taiwan microchip maker to announce a major high-tech expansion, further roiling one of the world's most competitive integrated-circuit markets.

Macronix, which acknowledged its first-half sales were well below target, said on Thursday it would invest more than T$200 billion (US$7.2 billion) within 10 years to build three or four advanced 12-inch wafer fabrication plants.
While huge, the Macronix plan is dwarfed by 10-year development plans unveiled in recent months by market leader Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co and number two United Microelectronics.
Taiwan Semicon pledged in April to spend T$400 billion on six advanced production lines in the new Tainan park, the biggest single investment in Taiwan to date.
Arch-rival United Micro went Taiwan Semicon one better in June, announcing a T$500 billion project to build 12-inch wafer fabs at Tainan.
Macronix said it soon would announce at least two major cooperation projects with foreign clients that would yield significant -- and badly needed -- new orders.

"Our negotiations with major foreign clients have almost reached maturity, and we will announce at least two deals within two months, which will bring us big orders," Macronix president Miin Wu told reporters.
"These clients are from the United States, Europe or Japan, all of which have huge purchasing power," Wu said.
Expressing confidence that such deals would yield orders, Wu said Macronix won US$110 million in 1996 orders from Nintendo Co Ltd after several years of cooperation.
Swift orders will be crucial if Macronix hopes to stand any chance of meeting its 1997 targets -- T$2.7 billion in net profit on T$14 billion sales.
"Due to worse-than-expected product price falls and foreign exchange losses of some T$200 million due to the weak yen, we only made sales of T$4 billion in the first half," Wu said.
"Our second half sales growth will be much stronger than the first half, but in our August review, lowering both our 1997 profit or sales targets is possible," he said.

He declined to identify Macronix' collaborative suitors, citing non-disclosure agreements, but said one Japanese client alone was in talks to cooperate on four separate sub-projects in technology development, design and memory chip development.
Wu said he was positive about the firm's 1998 performance and long-term outlook.
"Our sales in 1998 will have strong power to explode, and within 10 years we hope to become a world-class high-technology company in both sales and quality," he said.
Wu added that Macronix would not enter the semiconductor foundry business -- custom contract manufacturing -- like Taiwan Semiconductor and United Microelectronics.
"Foundry makers focus mostly on volume production, while Macronix specialises in design, closely matching our products with our clients in joint development," Wu said.
"Macronix will not concentrate on manufacturing; instead, we will try to offer total-solution services to clients -- which of course includes manufacturing."
Wu expressed some anxiety that so many Taiwanese firms were planning to build 12-inch wafer fabs.
"Taiwan's capability is not strong enough to lead the world trend, therefore so many Taiwan makers planning to enter the 12-inch wafer production is little bit too risky," he said.
